items.prompt: Why does this simple count-propagation proof exclude zero-weight links?

options.text: Dijkstra can never compute any distance when a weight is zero.
options.why: The issue here is the route-count dependency proof, not such a universal distance claim.

options.text: Zero weight can create equal-distance predecessor dependencies.
options.why: Strict positivity ensures every shortest predecessor is at a smaller distance before v propagates.

options.text: Zero is not representable as an exact Python integer.
options.why: It is exactly representable; the ordering argument is what changes.

options.text: Positive weights make every shortest route unique.
options.why: Several positive-weight routes can tie, and the function counts them.

items.explanation: Strict positivity ensures every shortest predecessor is at a smaller distance before v propagates.
